newsitem.title: USA: National Service to $287 mln in assets.
newsitem.headline: National Service to $287 mln in assets.

text.p: National Service Industries Inc said Monday it will sell plants and other assets representing about 40 percent of its textile rental volume for about $287 million.
The company said it had signed an agreement to sell 29 plants and related assets to G&K Services Inc, a supplier of corporate work uniform programs.
It said it expected to close the deal before August 31, the end of its fiscal year. The sale price is subject to adjustment after a post-closing audit, it added.
National Service said it will use the cash proceeds from the sale to invest in short-term markets and fund its share repurchase programs, among other things.
Although the company expects to record a pre-tax gain from the sale during its fourth quarter, it said the gain would likely be be offset by reserves.
National Service, which runs four businesses including lighting equipment, textile rental, specialty chemicals and envelopes, said the sale concluded a strategic review of its textile rental segment.
"As a result of the sale, (the company) will focus on improving the profitability of its core linen operations," it said.

"We believe it makes good business sense for (the company) to stay in the general linen markets, but only in those geographic areas and segments where the potential for future economic profit is clear," it added.
National Service said its remaining business will have about 60 percent of fiscal 1996's sales -- which totalled $531 million -- and 50 percent fewer assets.
